evidence.fact: water fit 82; soil health 69; heat and frost resilience 100; estimated revenue 29; animal feed value 44; pest and disease break 50
A crop is growing in about 6 of 12 months in a typical year.
Roots reach about 117 cm on average.
Based on 10 years of monthly weather (synthetic demonstration data).

benefits: Includes legumes (Chickpea). Legumes host bacteria that fix nitrogen from the air, which can reduce the nitrogen the next crop needs.
Every year of this plan fits within your yearly water budget.
Deeper roots can reach water and nutrients lower in the soil and help water soak in.
data_gaps: Weather and soil data are synthetic
Income compares estimated revenue per hectare, not profit. Production costs are not included.
Each crop uses one average water coefficient instead of stage-by-stage values.
Sowing windows, yields and prices are typical values, not your local calendar or market.
Soil values come from a regional dataset, not from samples of your own field.
Scores are modeled estimates, not certified results.
risks_needing_local_review: Water stress appears in 5 crop-months across the three years.
Barley is followed by Durum wheat, a crop from the same plant family, when the rotation repeats (year 3 to year 1). This can build up pests and diseases.
Check varieties, fertilizer and pest advice with your local agricultural advisor before changing your rotation.

reasons: Weather and soil data are synthetic
